analysis: Examined .github/scripts/test-threat-bedrock.py (base 1-585, head patch hunks @@-5,14 +5,15, @@-298 +299,83, @@-350 +428,74, @@-390 +536,25). The change is test-only CI tooling for the threat-review Bedrock scanner. The new tests assert that the workload call policy admits only planned calls plus one shared repair. They cover an emergency ceiling of 500 that defaults to 12 under the fixed policy, maxTokens 16384, a 600s read timeout with no SDK retries, and BEDROCK_WORKLOAD_LIMIT stops. Invalid policy, ceiling or token configs raise ReviewUnavailable before any request. The WorkloadScanTests cover large scans that finish integration, and the PolicyTests cover final incomplete results that require a human and never clear. None of this touches provider or coordinator runtime, attestation (TB-009/TB-011), the WebSocket contract (TB-002), encryption (A-001/A-003) or the provider assets. Billing-like cost bounds apply only to CI Bedrock spend, not to the platform payment ledger (A-009). The tests themselves add no attack surface. The implementation of BedrockCalls.plan_calls, Scanner and status_body lives in threat_review modules that were not supplied. The tests only assert the intended fail-closed bounds (no unplanned calls, no fallback spend, a ceiling that cannot be expanded). Whether the implementation enforces these bounds, and whether the merge gate's clean() still fails closed, must be verified in the integration pass against those modules. This is a coverage limit, not evidence of a regression. No threat-model update is needed for the provider scope.
